Pharvaris Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update

November 12, 2026

PDF Version

  * Deucrictibant IR NDA under review by the FDA with PDUFA date of April 23, 2027
  * Topline data from part 1 of CREAATE, a pivotal Phase 3 study evaluating deucrictibant XR for the prophylaxis of AAE-C1INH attacks, expected in 1Q2027; enrollment ongoing in part 2 of CREAATE evaluating deucrictibant IR for the on-demand treatment of AAE-C1INH attacks
  * Preparation of NDA dossier of deucrictibant XR for prophylaxis of AE-BK attacks ongoing; timeline remains on-track for submission in 1H2027
  * Strong financial position with cash and cash equivalents of €283 million as of September 30, 2026

ZUG, Switzerland, Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pharvaris (Nasdaq: PHVS), a late-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel, oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonists to help address unmet needs of those living with bradykinin-mediated angioedema (AE-BK), such as hereditary angioedema (HAE) and acquired angioedema due to C1 inhibitor deficiency (AAE-C1INH), today announced financial results for the third quarter ending on September 30, 2026, and provided a business update.

“The successful readout of the pivotal Phase 3 study of deucrictibant XR for the prophylaxis of HAE attacks was a major milestone for Pharvaris. If approved, deucrictibant could potentially address unmet needs across both on-demand and long-term prophylaxis of bradykinin-mediated angioedema attacks,” said Berndt Modig, Chief Executive Officer of Pharvaris. “Results of multiple data analyses from deucrictibant studies, including from CHAPTER-3, will be presented this weekend at the ACAAI Annual Scientific Meeting, providing the Pharvaris team with an excellent opportunity to engage with the scientific community of experts in the field of allergy and immunology. Additionally, our team is preparing for our potential first commercial launch and is well on its way to building an experienced commercial team.”

**Intellia Therapeutics Presents Additional Positive Clinical and Patient-Reported Data for Lonvoguran Ziclumeran (lonvo-z) at ACAAI 2026**

November 12, 2026

- Among patients previously on long-term prophylaxis (LTP) in HAELO Phase 3 trial, monthly attack rate decreased by 81% following lonvo-z dosing compared with prior LTP.
- 100% of patients receiving 50 mg of lonvo-z across Phase 1/2 clinical trial and HAELO were LTP-free as of the data cutoffs.
- Among 23 Phase 1/2 patients interviewed, all described their hereditary angioedema (HAE) as well controlled after receiving lonvo-z and 22 (96%) reported lonvo-z as an optimal HAE therapy.

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Intellia Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTLA), a leading biopharmaceutical company focused on revolutionizing medicine leveraging CRISPR gene editing and other core technologies, today announced highlights from its seven presentations at the American College of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology (ACAAI) 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting in Phoenix, Arizona. Intellia will host an investor webcast today at 10:00 a.m. ET to review certain data from the ACAAI presentations, share perspectives from key opinion leaders and discuss the company’s preparations for a planned commercial launch of lonvo-z in HAE.

## Oral Presentation Details:

### 1. Four-Year Durability/Safety of Lonvoguran Ziclumeran (Lonvo-z) 50 mg in Patients with Hereditary Angioedema

- **Title:** Four-Year Durability/Safety of Lonvoguran Ziclumeran (Lonvo-z) 50 mg in Patients with Hereditary Angioedema
- **Session:** Distinguished Industry and Late-Breaking Oral Abstracts – Session 2
- **Date and Time:** Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 4:43 – 4:53 p.m. MT
- **Presenter:** Danny Cohn, M.D., Ph.D., Associate Professor, Amsterdam University Medical Center, Department of Vascular Medicine, University of Amsterdam; Phase 1/2 and HAELO principal investigator

  - In the Phase 1/2 study, deep, consistent and durable reductions in plasma kallikrein were observed in all patients, with a mean reduction of 84% at four weeks that was maintained through up to four years of follow-up. Lonvo-z continues to be well tolerated with no new long-term risks identified.
  - Additional biomarkers were reported that support lonvo-z’s intended mechanism of action in which inactivation of the *KLKB1* gene and the associated reduction in plasma kallikrein protein leads to reduced activity of the kallikrein-kinin system and less bradykinin production.

### 2. Attack-Free and Long-Term Prophylaxis-Free Status Following Treatment with Lonvoguran Ziclumeran in Hereditary Angioedema

- **Title:** Attack-Free and Long-Term Prophylaxis-Free Status Following Treatment with Lonvoguran Ziclumeran in Hereditary Angioedema
- **Session:** Distinguished Industry and Late-Breaking Oral Abstracts – Session 2
- **Date and Time:** Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 4:53 – 5:03 p.m. MT
- **Presenter:** Emel Aygören-Pürsün, M.D., Department for Children and Adolescents, Angioedema Centre, University Hospital Frankfurt, Goethe University; Phase 1/2 and HAELO principal investigator

  - In the Phase 1/2 study (n=32), following a one-time 50 mg dose of lonvo-z, the proportion of patients who were attack-free after one year was at least 90% during each month with up to 4 years of follow-up. Additionally, 100% of patients were LTP-free as of the data cutoff.
  - The estimated probability of beginning an attack-free and LTP-free interval lasting ≥6 months increased from 81% at six months to 93% at 24 months post-dosing.

## Poster Presentation Details:

### 1. Lonvoguran Ziclumeran Demonstrated Consistent Benefit in All Hereditary Angioedema Patient Subgroups in Ph3 HAELO Study

# Pharvaris Presents Clinical and Real-World Data at the ACAAI 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting

November 12, 2026 10:28 ET  | Source: Pharvaris N.V. Pharvaris N.V.

  * Phase 3 CHAPTER-3 results to be presented in the Distinguished Industry and Late-breaking Oral Abstracts sessions on Saturday, November 14, from 4:30-6:00 p.m. MST
  * CHAPTER-3 met the primary and all secondary efficacy endpoints with statistical significance, confirming deucrictibant XR’s potential for the prevention of HAE attacks
  * Deucrictibant XR reduced the monthly attack rate by 83% in all HAE types and 87% in HAE Type 1 or 2 vs. placebo and was generally well tolerated

ZUG, Switzerland, Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Pharvaris (Nasdaq: PHVS), a late-stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel, oral bradykinin B2 receptor antagonists to help address unmet needs of those living with bradykinin-mediated diseases such as hereditary angioedema (HAE) and acquired angioedema due to C1 inhibitor deficiency (AAE-C1INH), summarized the oral and poster presentations at the American College of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology (ACAAI) 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting, taking place November 12-16, 2026, in Phoenix, Arizona. The presentations include late-breaking results from the Phase 3 CHAPTER-3 study evaluating investigational oral deucrictibant extended-release (XR) tablet for prophylaxis of HAE attacks to be presented in the Distinguished Industry and Late-breaking Oral Abstracts sessions on Saturday, November 14 from 4:30 – 6:00 p.m. MST, as well as final long-term results from the prophylaxis Phase 2 open-label extension, additional analyses of the pivotal Phase 3 on-demand treatment study, clinical pharmacology data supporting the potential combined use of the XR and immediate-release (IR) formulations, a comprehensive assessment of deucrictibant’s cardiovascular safety across the development program, and the real-world economic burden of HAE.

“This first opportunity to share CHAPTER-3 primary data with the medical community in the setting of a large scientific conference represents an important milestone in deucrictibant’s clinical development, with once-daily oral deucrictibant XR demonstrating reductions in the HAE attack rate in the range of those observed with injectable long-term prophylactic therapies, and nearly half of participants remaining attack-free over the entire 24-week treatment period,” said Peng Lu, M.D., Ph.D., President of Pharvaris. “When considered alongside the wealth of data being presented at ACAAI across our on-demand and prophylaxis clinical programs, as well as data exploring the economic burden of HAE to the healthcare system, these findings strengthen our belief in deucrictibant’s potential to address unmet needs and to change how people living with bradykinin-mediated angioedema manage their disease. Our ambition is to provide the community with effective and well-tolerated oral treatment options designed with the objective of addressing patients’ needs, whether to prevent attacks or to treat them when they occur, and ultimately to lessen the impact of this unpredictable disease on everyday life and healthcare systems.”

# Deucrictibant (PHVS416) - (CHAPTER-3)

Pharvaris N.V.PHVS

Indication
    Hereditary angioedema - prophylactic use

Stage
    phase3

Event
    Phase 3

Details
    

November 12, 2026: Pharvaris (NASDAQ: PHVS) outlined ACAAI 2026 presentations for deucrictibant in hereditary angioedema (HAE), including late-breaking Phase 3 CHAPTER-3 data on once-daily oral deucrictibant XR for prophylaxis, to be presented November 14.

Deucrictibant XR / CHAPTER-3 (Phase 3, prophylaxis): In 85 HAE patients randomized 2:1 to XR 40 mg or placebo for 24 weeks, monthly attack rate was reduced 83% across all HAE types (p<0.0001) and 87% in a post hoc analysis of HAE type 1 or 2. Treated on-demand attacks fell 83% and moderate-to-severe attacks 77% versus placebo. Among XR-treated patients, 98%, 96%, and 65% achieved at least 50%, 70%, and 90% attack-rate reductions, and 45% were attack-free for 24 weeks. The study met its primary and all secondary efficacy endpoints; XR was generally well tolerated with no treatment-related serious or cardiovascular adverse events.

CHAPTER-1 OLE (Phase 2): Final long-term prophylaxis results showed a 92.4% average attack-rate reduction from trial baseline, with mean monthly attacks of 0.12 versus 2.18 at baseline, sustained through about 34 months.

RAPIDe-3 / deucrictibant IR (Phase 3, on-demand): Median time to end of progression was 17.47 minutes versus more than 3.5 hours for placebo; >95% of attacks maintained relief/resolution, and >80% did so with a single capsule.

Other ACAAI presentations cover XR+IR PK/safety modeling, an integrated cardiovascular safety review across 25 studies (>740 exposed participants), and a U.S. claims analysis showing substantial HAE healthcare utilization and costs.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
